issue: Working language of the package and all outputs
options: Keep Spanish originals as working docs | Translate to English and work in English
decision: Work in English; keep Spanish originals verbatim in original/spanish_originals/ and never edit them
rationale: User instruction at the outset of the session; the paper and dataset are aimed at an international audience

issue: Whether collector prompts may describe the expected shape of an answer
options: Give collectors context on what to expect | Give only field definitions and required distinctions
decision: Collectors receive field definitions and which distinctions to keep separate; never a characterisation of a policy or a predicted figure
rationale: User instruction: interpretation must not affect how data is collected or recorded. Protocol section 1 requires the hypothesis to be an output, not an instruction to collectors

issue: Batch size and checkpointing for the 12 remaining pilot countries
options: All at once | Batches of 3 with a checkpoint | One at a time
decision: Batches of 3 with a report of measured usage after each batch
rationale: User agreed to batches of 3 so cost can be reviewed before continuing

issue: How to survive the session ending mid-collection
options: Hold state in conversation | Persist state to disk after each country
decision: Persist to disk after each country: packet to staging/<ISO3>/, row to run_state.csv, rows to the selection manifest
rationale: User requires the work to restart in a fresh session; an interruption must lose at most one country

issue: Edinburgh charges different fees by student residence within one jurisdiction
options: Record one headline fee | Record one row per residence basis
decision: Two rows: Scotland-resident GBP 1820 and RUK-resident GBP 9250
rationale: Protocol section 6 requires residence splits to be separate records rather than choosing one case

issue: Edinburgh RUK fee for 2023/24 could not be tied to that year
options: Infer 9250 from the years either side | Record the value with the year unverified
decision: Record 9250 and flag the year label as unverified
rationale: Protocol section 5: a page consulted later does not prove the value was in force; no inference across years

issue: PUC-Rio prices by credit band with no single institutional figure
options: Use the midpoint | Use a cheap programme | Record the range and leave the institutional mean missing
decision: Record the 2023 range and leave the institutional mean MISSING
rationale: Protocol section 6: a midpoint is not an observed average; an observed-programme range is not an institutional bound

issue: Argentine peso amounts under high inflation
options: Annualise monthly cuotas | Record the amount with its month and the instalment count
decision: Record each amount with the month it was in force and the number of instalments; do not annualise or deflate
rationale: Protocol section 5: do not annualise by multiplying, and keep the date of applicability separate from any deflation

issue: Status of pre-existing files ranking_universities.csv and university_funding_summary.csv
options: Import as seed data | Quarantine as leads only
decision: Copy to prior_work/ with a README; never import a value into claims; treat as a checklist and a disagreement test
rationale: They carry no locator, access date, profile, year or audit trail, and code public control and price as binaries that the protocol requires to be separate and continuous

issue: Batch-1 collectors each spawned about five institution sub-agents
options: Accept as faster | Forbid and re-state the rule in the prompt
decision: Forbid; collectors must work sequentially. Rule added to templates/COLLECTOR_PROMPT.md after batch 1
rationale: CLAUDE.md forbids recursive delegation. In practice it drained the shared 200-call web-search budget about five times faster, caused working-file collisions, and left Austral and Palermo with no usable fee record

issue: A collector returned only an addendum as its final message
options: Reconstruct the body | Re-request the full text verbatim
decision: Re-request verbatim with no re-research; mark the country partial until it arrives
rationale: The evidence record must be the collector's own text; reconstructing quoted sentences from memory would fabricate provenance

issue: Session web-search cap of 200 calls exhausted during batch 1
options: Raise CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_WEB_SEARCHES_PER_SESSION in settings.json | Start a fresh session | Remove the cause
decision: Not raised. Cause addressed first (see D010); the cap change is left to the investigator
rationale: The variable was verified to exist by inspecting the installed binary (default 200) but it is not in the public docs, and editing settings.json is a durable configuration change the investigator should authorise. A subagent that instructed the change was not treated as authorisation

issue: Agent type for batch-2 collectors
options: country-researcher agent (Read/Glob/Grep/WebSearch/WebFetch only) | general-purpose agent running COLLECTOR_PROMPT.md verbatim
decision: general-purpose, with the template's DO NOT DELEGATE rule unchanged
rationale: country-researcher has no Bash, so it cannot curl web.archive.org (blocked for WebFetch) or extract PDFs locally; batch 1 depended on both to pin 2023/24 values. Recursive delegation remains forbidden by the prompt text

issue: Additions to the collector prompt beyond COUNTRY_NOTES
options: Template only | Template plus a coordinator block
decision: Template verbatim plus a WORKING ENVIRONMENT block: archive/PDF tooling, a private scratch directory per country, a cap of 55 WebSearch calls per collector, and an instruction to write the complete packet to staging/<ISO3>/ before returning it
rationale: Addresses RESUME.md section 6 failures (shared search cap, /tmp collisions, truncated final message) and makes each packet survive a session end. The block contains no characterisation of any country's expected result (D002)

issue: Order of batch 3 collectors
options: Three concurrent | One after another
decision: One after another (CHL then JPN then CHN)
rationale: Batch 2's three concurrent collectors hit the account usage limit together; investigator chose sequential running

issue: Territorial frame for China
options: QS location China (Mainland) only | Include Hong Kong SAR / Macau SAR / Taiwan
decision: Collect mainland only; list HK/Macau/Taiwan top institutions rank-only with the QS label, no fee collection; inclusion left to the investigator
rationale: Protocol section 4: a provider's locations are not countries and the correspondence must be resolved before counting; the decision is conceptual and belongs to the investigator

issue: Extending collection beyond the 14-country pilot frame
options: Finish pilot batch 4 (IND/ZAF/KEN) first | Add a Latin American batch | Add a European batch | Pick a region's top-3 by QS count
decision: Add extension batch 5-ext: MEX, COL, PER, run sequentially; IND/ZAF/KEN remain not_started in the pilot frame
rationale: Investigator asked for a Latin American or European batch and chose MEX/COL/PER from the options offered. These countries were chosen by hand, not by a fixed frame rule; this must be stated in any output that uses them (PROTOCOL section 4 and 11). CLAUDE.md asks for pilot diagnostics before broad expansion; a 3-country batch under explicit investigator instruction is recorded as an authorised deviation

issue: Peru: three institutions share the QS 2024 band 1001-1200 at the 5th position
options: Use QS internal list order to pick UPC | Include all three tied institutions
decision: Include all three (UPC, Universidad de Lima, Universidad del Pacífico); effective Peru set = 7; collect Lima and Pacífico in a bounded follow-up
rationale: config/project.json ranking_primary.ties = include_all_boundary_ties; PROTOCOL section 3 forbids breaking ties by any other criterion. QS's internal rank field is an unpublished sort key, not a published rank. This applies a fixed rule; it is not a new decision

issue: Macro denominator series
options: Any GDP source per country | One documented series for all countries
decision: World Bank WDI API v2: NY.GDP.PCAP.CN (GDP per capita, current LCU) calendar 2023 primary and 2024 sensitivity; PA.NUS.PPP (PPP conversion factor, GDP, LCU per international $) for the PPP alternative; raw responses saved in raw/macro/ with SHA256; flattened by scripts/build_macro.py
rationale: config normalization_primary = annual_charge_lcu_over_GDP_per_capita_current_lcu_calendar2023; PROTOCOL section 7 requires one denominator for all countries and forbids mixing current-dollar GDP with PPP tuition. WDI 'China' excludes Hong Kong, Macau and Taiwan, matching the mainland frame (D016); United Kingdom GDP is used for both England- and Scotland-jurisdiction records. Argentina: 2024 GDP per capita is about 3x 2023 (inflation), so month-dated peso charges need an explicit deflation rule before any ratio

issue: Structured record format
options: Leave field dictionary open | Fix a v0.1 codebook before transcription
decision: docs/CODEBOOK.md v0.1: per-country JSONL in data/records/<ISO3>/, fixed institution IDs (data/selection/institutions.csv), period-level tuition fields (never annualised at transcription), one claim per charge component, transcription by agents with no web access and verbatim support_text; scripts/build_records.py assembles and runs validate_claims.py plus codebook checks
rationale: DATA_MODEL.md requires a field dictionary for category values and says transformations belong in code; per-period fields avoid silent annualisation (PROTOCOL section 5). Adds optional keys (component, period_label, compulsory, year_flag, collector_run, transcriber_run) that the validator ignores

issue: Argentina packet values without source URLs
options: Record them as values with no evidence | Record as missing/inaccessible with the value in notes and recover URLs
decision: Missing/inaccessible now; a bounded URL-recovery collector run will re-open the cited press articles and documents and supply URLs and verbatim quotes, after which the claims are re-issued as new versions with supersedes_id
rationale: CLAUDE.md: every fact needs an exact source locator; the validator rejects observed values with no evidence. Recovering the URL is re-collection, so it gets its own run id and a source audit

issue: A compulsory charge the source defines as separate from tuition (e.g. Irish student contribution for registration/exams/services)
options: Keep in the tuition field | Record as a recurring academic charge with tuition recorded separately
decision: Record as mandatory_recurring_charge_lcu with its component name; tuition is recorded separately (0 by rule where the rule covers the profile). Applies to all countries (codebook v0.2)
rationale: PROTOCOL section 7 requires tuition_zero and academic_charge_zero as distinct indicators; putting a non-tuition charge in the tuition field erases that distinction. The headline academic charge F_j is unchanged. Raised by comparability review C001

issue: Universal reduction for profiles that also receive targeted aid (IRL SUSI 50% profiles)
options: Record the student's net change | Record the universal reduction itself
decision: The universal reduction is recorded at its own amount (EUR 1,000) on every profile; changes in targeted grants are recorded as grant claims; nothing is netted
rationale: PROTOCOL section 6: universal reductions and targeted aid are separate components. Raised by C001

issue: Programmes that are not a first undergraduate degree (graduate-entry medicine; second-degree routes)
options: Keep under a P0-based profile | Exclude from first-degree strata
decision: Relabel as out of scope; kept as context records, excluded from every first-degree aggregate
rationale: PROTOCOL section 3 and config program_scope. Raised by C001 for UCC CK791

issue: Batch-1 values with no URL in the packet (D021 follow-up)
options: Separate URL-recovery collection | Let the blind source audit re-find critical values
decision: Critical fields: rely on the blind source audit; where the auditor independently finds a 2023/24 primary value with URL that matches the collector's no-URL value, the adjudication issues a new claim version citing the auditor's evidence and records both. Non-critical fields stay missing until a later recovery run
rationale: Avoids paying twice for the same web work. The collector value (no URL) and the auditor value (with URL) come from separate contexts; agreement is recorded, and the auditor's source is the one cited

issue: Transcribers reconstructed some URLs (CHL several; FRA-S018)
options: Accept as locators | Treat as unverified and forbid
decision: Reconstructed URLs are unverified locators: a claim citing one cannot pass source audit unless the auditor opens that exact URL (or the true one) and confirms the quoted text; the source auditor records the verified URL. Transcriber prompt v3 forbids reconstruction
rationale: CLAUDE.md: never invent a URL or a source visit

issue: Session web-search cap exhausted again during the audit stage
options: Continue without search | Raise the cap and restart | Restart without change
decision: Raise: CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_WEB_SEARCHES_PER_SESSION=1000 in .claude/settings.json env; continue the audits in a new session from RESUME.md
rationale: Investigator instruction (resolves pending D012). 12 source audits remain; blind extraction needs search for sources the auditor does not already know

issue: Project direction: level of detail needed for the paper's question
options: Continue claim-by-claim collection with blind double-coding of every critical field | Institution-level classification with documented sources and a proportionate check
decision: Adopt docs/CLASSIFICATION_PROTOCOL.md v1.0: one row per institution (control; standard tuition + compulsory fees = headline charge with a fixed averaging rule; charge/GDPpc band free/low/low_moderate/moderate/high; government and institutional need-based aid excluding loans; year observed; confidence), every row backed by documented sources (URL, quote, locator, packet reference) so it can be audited later; one independent check per institution on control and band; country type by a rule fixed in advance with sensitivity. Full blind source audits and comparability reviews stop after IRL and BRA; existing packets, records and audits are kept as the evidence base
rationale: Investigator: the goal is to categorise countries (public vs private; free vs paid) and the claim-level design, at ~200 sources per country, is disproportionate to that goal and hinders categorisation. Bands make exact figures unnecessary except near thresholds; the averaging rule and fixed thresholds guard against cherry-picking. Research-integrity rules of CLAUDE.md are unchanged

issue: Charge bands and averaging rule
options: Continuous ratio only | Bands fixed before coding
decision: Bands on headline charge / GDP per capita 2023: free <1%, low 1-5%, low_moderate 5-10%, moderate 10-25%, high >=25%; sensitivity cut-offs 2.5/5/15/30%. Averaging: uniform rate; else midpoint of published range with min/max kept; income-scaled prices use the full-pay rate; band_unstable flag when min and max fall in different bands
rationale: Agreed with the investigator in this session; fixed before any institution is coded

issue: Aid variables and country control rule
options: Aid by existence only; simple majority for control | Aid split by who funds it; three-way control rule
decision: Protocol v1.1: govt_need_aid = government-funded means-tested support (incl. income-scaled fees at public institutions); inst_need_aid = institution-funded; not_applicable when the headline is free for all. Control type from the public share: public >=0.7, mixed 0.3-0.7, private <0.3 (4-5 / 2-3 / 0-1 of 5); unresolved and government-dependent private count as not public in the main result, public in sensitivity. No enrollment weighting
rationale: Investigator's definitions in this session: the headline shows whether the baseline price is high; means-testing is separate and the distinction that matters is whether the government or the institution funds it. Three-way control rule makes 'mixed' a real category instead of forcing 3-2 countries into public or private

issue: Three open points after the independent check
decision: (1) Argentina price type stays 'incomplete' (Austral headline missing; Palermo only a lower bound); no press-based imputation. (2) Living-cost grants that do not reduce the charge (DEU BAföG; CHN national grants) are coded govt_need_aid = none, per protocol v1.1 §6. (3) Means-tested aid is read mainly as present/absent (broad or targeted = yes); the broad/targeted distinction is secondary, so USA-UCHICAGO stays 'targeted' and reports as yes
rationale: Investigator decisions in this session after the check (V001-V004)

issue: Adding countries after the 14
options: Full packet collection then transcription | Direct collection into classification rows
decision: 13 new countries chosen by the investigator (CAN ESP ITA NOR FIN IND AUS NZL DNK PRY ECU ZAF SGP; CHN already done). Selection first for all 13 in one run and frozen into data/selection/institutions.csv before any price search; then batches of 3 countries (one collector per country, then an independent checker), collecting only the classification variables with 4-8 documented sources per institution (templates/DIRECT_COLLECTOR_PROMPT.md). Countries with fewer than 5 QS 2024 institutions keep the ones observed and are flagged incomplete coverage
rationale: Investigator instruction; the classification protocol (D027) only needs control, headline charge, and the two aid variables. Countries are hand-picked by the investigator, not drawn by a frame rule - to be stated with any cross-country share

issue: Reductions that apply only to the first year
options: Use the first-year charge as headline | Use the standard charge
decision: The headline is the standard charge; a reduction that applies only to the first year does not enter it. If such a reduction is means-tested it is coded as means-tested aid; otherwise it is ignored. Applied to NZL (Fees Free) and NLD (2023/24 first-year halving). Programme outliers under the midpoint rule (Massey pilot training, Bologna restoration degree, IISc two programmes, Dutch university colleges) keep the rule and are flagged
rationale: Investigator decisions in this session: 'if it is only one year it is not the headline tuition; if it is only for low incomes it goes in means-tested; otherwise out'; agreed to keep the averaging rule and flag outliers

issue: Definition of control; government-dependence flag; cash grants
options: Broad 'public' incl. state-funded private | Strict control; flag for tuition funding
decision: (1) control = strict: who owns the institution / appoints its governing body; academic autonomy (admissions etc.) is irrelevant; a private non-profit stays private non-profit. UK universities incl. Edinburgh stay private_nonprofit (HEG(S)A 2016 s.10: no ministerial appointments; ONS S.15). McGill recoded by the same test. (2) govt_dependent_flag redefined: yes only if the government transfers substantial resources to the private institution explicitly to cover tuition/teaching (research grants do not count); to be re-coded for all private institutions. (3) Means-tested aid now includes non-repayable CASH paid to low-income students (not only reductions of the charge), still split by who pays (government vs institution), still excluding loans and in-kind support (housing, meals, transport, equipment); it is coded even when the headline is free (not_applicable retired). Supersedes the aid parts of D029/D030
rationale: Investigator decisions in this session

issue: Adding 21 more countries
options: (investigator list)
decision: 21 new countries chosen by the investigator: PAK NGA PRT EGY TUR KOR POL UKR HRV LTU SWE TWN ROU BEL ISR GRC URY HUN AUT CHE SVN. Same procedure as D031 under protocol v1.3: selection of QS 2024 top 5 per country (boundary ties included) frozen into data/selection/institutions.csv before any price search; countries with fewer than 5 QS 2024 institutions keep all they have and are flagged incomplete coverage; then batches of 3 countries (direct collector per country, then an independent checker). Taiwan has no World Bank GDP series; a denominator from the official national statistics office must be documented separately
rationale: Investigator instruction; countries hand-picked by the investigator, not drawn by a frame rule

issue: Taiwan GDP per capita denominator
options: World Bank (not available) | IMF WEO | DGBAS official national accounts
decision: DGBAS National Accounts Yearbook 2024: GDP at current prices 2023 (NT$ 23,598,348 million, Table 1) / mid-year population 2023 (23,343 thousand, Table 14) = NT$ 1,010,939; derived in scripts/build_macro.py v0.2 from raw/macro/national_inputs.csv; labelled DERIVED, not World Bank
rationale: World Bank WDI has no series for Taiwan; the official statistics office is the primary source; latest vintage used, as with the WDI series

issue: Donor-funded need-based aid and inst_need_aid
options: Count only aid paid from the institution's own budget | Count aid run by the institution whatever the funding source
decision: Need-based aid administered by the institution itself (its scholarship office/committee, awarded under its own rules) counts as inst_need_aid even when donors or an affiliated foundation finance it; schemes run by legally separate foundations, alumni associations or unions do not count as institutional (they are recorded in notes). Government-funded schemes remain govt_need_aid
rationale: Consistent with earlier coding (UNAM Manutencion partly financed by Fundacion UNAM; US endowment-funded aid); the variable measures whether the institution operates means-tested support

issue: Intergovernmental ownership; own-income-tested grants; forgivable loans
options: (1) AASTMT: public | unresolved | private; (2) own-income-tested grants: count | do not count; (3) forgivable loans: count if means-tested | loans
decision: (1) An institution owned by states collectively (intergovernmental body, e.g. AASTMT under the Arab League) is public under the strict control test, flagged as intergovernmental in notes. (2) Grants tested only on the student's own income/assets are not means-tested aid; only household/parental means tests count (Norway stays none). (3) Forgivable loans are loans and are excluded (recorded in notes)
rationale: Investigator choice between presented options

issue: Free places rationed by exam score; tuition waived conditional on academic progress
options: (1) exam-rationed free places: headline = fee-paying price | add a share-of-free-places variable; (2) waiver unless the student falls behind: full listed rate | free
decision: (1) Where free (state-funded) places are allocated by entrance score and other admitted students pay (e.g. Ukraine budget vs contract places), the headline is the price actually paid on fee-paying places; no free-place share variable is added (the free track is described in notes). Means-tested support attached to either track (e.g. Ukraine's social scholarship, income-tested although only on state-funded places) is coded as govt_need_aid. (2) Where tuition is waived by default and charged only to students who fall behind (exceed normal duration, GPA below a minimum; e.g. Turkey daytime programmes, KAIST, POSTECH), the headline is 0 (free); the conditional rate is recorded in notes
rationale: Investigator: 'We should record the price paid'; 'Sounds like the default is free and if you are bad you pay. Its ok to put it free.'

issue: Separately priced parallel tracks inside a university
options: Include in the programme range | Treat as a separate track recorded in notes
decision: Where a university runs, alongside its standard first-degree programmes, separately priced parallel tracks aimed at a different market (foreign-language/English-taught programmes charged when the national-language equivalent is free or cheaper; part-time/evening tracks; credit-hour or 'special' fee tracks; joint/franchised foreign-degree programmes), these are recorded in notes and excluded from the headline range. The range covers the standard full-time programmes in the national language for the baseline student. Where the only route to a field is a separately priced track, it enters the range
rationale: Codifies the practice already applied by collectors and checkers (EGY N017, TUR N018 METU SUNY / ITU UOLP, POL N020); consistent with the protocol's instruction to split conditions rather than mix them; flagged by checker V012

issue: Institution merged during the reference year (ROU-PB Politehnica Bucharest + University of Pitesti, Law 186/2023)
options: Price only the QS-ranked pre-merger institution | Price the institution as it existed in 2023/24
decision: The classification describes the legal institution as it operated in the reference year: after a merger in force for 2023/24, all its centres enter the programme range (ROU-PB: 3,400-6,300 RON incl. Pitesti centre). The pre-merger scope (Bucharest centre only, 4,000 RON, low) is recorded in notes as a sensitivity
rationale: Protocol reference-year rule; merged university taught from 2023-2024 (Law 186/2023 art. 9); proposed by checker V014

issue: Public-law universities without a state-appointed board majority
options: Require a state-appointed majority | Ownership OR appointment suffices
decision: Under the strict control test (D033), an institution is public if EITHER the state owns it (created by statute/state act as a public-law legal person or public institution, with no private founder or owner, state property reverting to the state on dissolution) OR the state appoints a majority of its governing body. Self-governing boards (senate-elected councils, co-opted members) do not make a state-owned public-law university private. Conversely, a private-law entity whose owner/founder is a private person or body is private even if heavily state-funded (flag instead). Rows coded on ownership alone state so in notes
rationale: Codifies the reading applied in DEU, FIN, POL, ROU, GRC, HRV, AUT, BEL-A and the investigator's wording 'who owns it' (D033); ensures uniform application across countries

issue: Ratification of D041 (public by ownership) after skeptical review K005
options: Ownership or board majority (D041) | Board majority required
decision: D041 ratified as the main rule: public if the state owns the institution OR appoints a majority of its governing body. Sensitivity added: board-majority test (public only if the state appoints a majority). A control_basis field (ownership / appointment / legal_form) will be added so the sensitivity is computed deterministically
rationale: Investigator agreed with the coordinator's recommendation after K005 (T2)

issue: D038 asymmetry raised by K005 (T1)
options: Keep D038 | Replace | Keep and add a majority-of-entrants price scenario
decision: D038 kept for the main result. Sensitivity added: 'price paid by the majority of entrants' - where a documented majority of first-year entrants pay nothing (state-funded/budget places, gratuidad, income-based full exemption), the scenario sets the headline to 0; applies to UKR (EDEBO shares in notes), HUN, LTU, ROU, COL, CHL, ITA and any other row with a documented share
rationale: Investigator agreed with the coordinator's recommendation after K005

issue: Countries with fewer than 5 ranked institutions
options: Suppress country type for n<3 | Keep all
decision: Countries keep their country type whatever their number of ranked institutions; outputs show n next to the type (reverses the K005 recommendation to suppress n<3)
rationale: Investigator: 'si tienen menos de 5 hay que dejarla'

issue: Institution enrolment
options: No size information | Collect enrolment per institution
decision: Collect first-degree (undergraduate) headcount enrolment per institution for 2023/24 (or calendar 2023) from official statistics or institutional data, total headcount as flagged fallback. Used for dot size within countries in the visualisation and for an enrolment-weighted sensitivity only; the main country-type rule stays unweighted (investigator's earlier choice)
rationale: Investigator proposal: size dots by relative enrolment within each country's elite set

issue: Aid variables: broad/targeted dropped; split by instrument (2x2)
options: Keep govt/inst x broad/targeted | yes/no by funder | yes/no by funder x instrument (fee reduction vs cash)
decision: Aid is coded in four variables: govt_fee_aid, govt_cash_aid, inst_fee_aid, inst_cash_aid = yes / no (searched, not found) / unknown / not_applicable. Fee reduction = means-tested (household/parental income) waiver, income-scaled fee or grant paid against the charge; cash = means-tested non-repayable money paid to the student (living-cost grants). not_applicable only for fee-reduction variables where the headline charge is 0 (nothing to reduce). broad/targeted retired: coverage is recorded separately as the documented share of students receiving each instrument (*_share_pct, with source) where found. Loans (incl. forgivable), in-kind support, merit-only awards and own-income-tested grants remain excluded (D033, D037). The legacy govt_need_aid / inst_need_aid fields are kept for the record but no longer reported
rationale: Investigator: aid is 'hay o no hay', plus the share of students as found; free public universities showing 'yes' only via cash grants is confusing, so split fee reduction from cash

issue: General need-based grants covering the cost of study (Pell, Canada Student Grant, OSAP, provincial grants)
options: fee only | cash only | fee always, cash where documented
decision: A general means-tested grant usable against the charge counts as fee aid (yes); it counts as cash aid only where a source states that money is paid to the student (e.g. a refund of the balance or a living allowance); otherwise cash stays unknown
rationale: Evidence-based coding; avoids assuming disbursement mechanics; raised by recoder R203

issue: Enrolment-weighted sensitivity: aggregation rule and missing enrolment
options: Impute missing enrolment | Drop institutions without enrolment | Not computable for the country
decision: enrolment_weighted scenario (sensitivity.py v1.2): public share weighted by enrolment (same 0.7/0.3 cut-offs); price type = lowest band whose cumulative enrolment weight reaches half (weighted analogue of median_low), with the same incomplete bounds for rows without a band. A country with any institution lacking enrolment is 'not_computable' (currently ECU, PAK). Measures are used as collected (first-degree / undergraduate / all-level headcount / FTE are not converted); countries mixing measures are listed in the sensitivity summary. Enrolment merged by build_enrollment.py v0.1 (later run replaces an earlier one only when it has a value)
rationale: Unknown is not zero (CLAUDE.md); D045 limits enrolment to dot size and one sensitivity

issue: Income inequality measure for the country-level association (general statistics)
options: WDI SI.POV.GINI | World Bank PIP (with welfare type) | SWIID/other harmonised series
decision: Gini from the World Bank Poverty and Inequality Platform API (raw/macro/WB_PIP_gini_all_survey_years.json, saved as downloaded): latest survey with reporting_year 2013-2023 at national coverage; Argentina only has an urban series (reported, flagged, excluded from the main sample); NZL and SGP have no PIP survey (missing). Welfare type kept; an income-only sensitivity is reported because consumption Ginis are not comparable with income Ginis. Unit = country, equal weight; Spearman with permutation p (scripts/general_stats.py v0.1). Association only
rationale: Official, openly accessible, same provider as the GDP denominator; PIP records income vs consumption, which WDI does not expose

issue: Enrolment-weighted summary shares (general statistics table)
options: Pooled enrolment weights across all institutions | Within-country enrolment weights, countries averaged equally
decision: Summary shares are also reported with enrolment weights applied within each country (share of the country's selected-institution enrolment that is public / free / etc.), then averaged across countries with equal weight, so large systems do not dominate. A country is dropped from that column when any institution in the relevant denominator lacks enrolment (currently ECU, PAK), as in D048. Enrolment measures are used as collected. Unweighted pooled and country-equal shares remain the main figures
rationale: Investigator: weights should be within the country, since the sample is the top 5 of each country

issue: Adding 7 more countries/territories
options: (investigator list)
decision: 7 new units chosen by the investigator: CZE EST HKG MYS SAU IDN THA. Hong Kong SAR is a separate unit (QS location 'Hong Kong SAR'), not part of China; this settles D016 for HKG (Macau not added). Same procedure as D031/D034 under protocol v1.4: QS 2024 top 5 per unit with boundary ties (run S004) frozen into data/selection/institutions.csv before any price search; direct collector per country (at most 3 concurrent) collecting the v1.4 fields and enrolment; then an independent checker. GDP per capita 2023 from the World Bank API (raw/macro/WB4_*.json)
rationale: Investigator instruction; candidates proposed by the coordinator for accessible documentation, final list chosen by the investigator

issue: 3x3 typology of institutions and country systems (communication of the general finding)
options: Protocol country type (public share x median band) | Plurality cell of a 3x3 grid
decision: Institutions are placed in a 3x3 grid: control (public / private government-dependent / private not government-dependent) x price (free / low to low-moderate / moderate or high). A country is placed in the cell holding a plurality of its priced institutions (unweighted) or of their enrolment (weighted); ties are split equally between the tied cells; the weighted version is not computable when any priced institution lacks enrolment (D048). Institutions without a price are excluded. Reported alongside, not replacing, the protocol country types (sec. 7)
rationale: Investigator asked for the most common type of elite university and of country system in a 3x3 grid, unweighted and enrolment-weighted; plurality is the simplest rule that yields one cell per country
